title: No interest on late payment
rule: Raise when the contract says no interest is payable on late payment (High), or is silent (unclear).
value_found: no interest is payable on late payment: 'No interest payable on any payment due or awarded'
reference_value: NHAI pays Bank Rate + 3% on unpaid sums; CPWD pays 5% simple interest after 45 days.
reference_source: NHAI EPC agreement cl. 19.9 [SEEN]; CPWD GCC 2023 cl. 7 [SEEN]; 'no interest' seen in the MP tender [SEEN]
quote: 23. No Interest Payable No interest shall be payable to the Contractor on any payment due or awarded by
explanation: The contract says no interest is payable on late payment: 'No interest payable on any payment due or awarded'. If the employer pays late you carry the cost on your overdraft and cannot claim interest. Every month of late payment is a straight loss.

title: Progress-linked termination or heavy withholding
rule: Raise when the employer may terminate on slow progress or once damages hit the cap, or withholds large percentages for missed milestones.
value_found: termination penalty adds 20% of value of work not completed; Milestone slippage: amount retained of 2.5%, 5%, 7.5% or 10% of the work remaining unexecuted (by slippage band)
reference_value: Milestone withholding refunded when progress is made good; termination only for real default.
reference_source: Seen in the MP tender (Annexure P) and the MoEF tender (Schedule F) [SEEN]; 1% line [ASSUMPTION]
quote: Penalty for not establishing field Laboratory 1% of Contract Amount per month, subject to a maximum of Rs. 50,000/- per month of
explanation: The employer can end the contract when progress or damages pass a limit (termination penalty adds 20% of value of work not completed). On termination you also risk losing your securities, so a bad patch can become a total loss. Missed milestones lead to money being held back (Milestone slippage: amount retained of 2.5%, 5%, 7.5% or 10% of the work remaining unexecuted (by slippage band)). Cash you expected can stop mid-contract; it is usually refunded only if you catch up. Money at stake: about Rs 18.86 lakh (largest withholding % x contract value).

title: Retention or security deposit high or uncapped
rule: Raise when the total retention cap is above 5% of contract value, or there is no cap, or all retention is held to the end of the defects period with no stage release.
value_found: Refunded on completion of defect liability period
reference_value: Security deposit usually 5% of each running bill, replaceable by a bank guarantee; half released at taking-over.
reference_source: Manual for Procurement of Works 2022, Dept. of Expenditure [SEEN]
quote: 30.3 The Security deposits shall be refunded of completion of defect liability period. The
explanation: All retention is held to the end of the defects period ('Refunded on completion of defect liability period'), with none released at completion. The reference practice releases half at taking-over. Plan to finance this money for the full defects period, or offer a bank guarantee instead. Money at stake: about Rs 9.43 lakh (largest retention held, from the cash model).

title: Performance security high
rule: Raise when performance security is above 5% of value, or an additional security for low bids applies.
value_found: Additional performance security if the bid is more than 15% below the estimate: contract amount times the difference between the bid perc...
reference_value: Usually 5% of contract value; Dept. of Expenditure order of 12 Nov 2020 cut it to 3%.
reference_source: Manual for Procurement of Works 2022 [SEEN]; DoE OM 12 Nov 2020 [SEEN, via a circular that quotes it]
quote: Additional Performance Security, if any Equal to an amount arrived at, by multiplying the contract amount with difference of percentage between percent rates (below/minus) of successful bid and 15% percent (below/minus), considering bid rates less than Fifteen percent
explanation: An extra security applies on top of the normal guarantee: Additional performance security if the bid is more than 15% below the estimate: contract amount times the difference between the bid perc.... If your bid is well below the estimate you must lock up more bank limit; price this into an aggressive bid. Money at stake: about Rs 9.43 lakh (performance security x contract value).

title: Slow or unclear payment
rule: Raise when the period to pay a bill is above 30 days, or is not stated.
value_found: NOT_STATED: silent (nothing found after a full search)
reference_value: NHAI pays within 30 days; CPWD part payment in 10 and the rest in 28 working days.
reference_source: NHAI EPC agreement cl. 19.9 [SEEN]; CPWD GCC 2023 cl. 7 [SEEN]; 30-day line [ASSUMPTION]
explanation: The contract does not say how many days the employer has to pay a bill. You cannot plan your cash, and late payment is hard to challenge.

title: No advance, or a costly one
rule: Raise when there is no mobilisation advance, or the advance carries interest, or its guarantee is above 100% of the advance.
value_found: No mobilisation and construction machinery advance is payable
reference_value: Advance should be need-based; interest-free advances are discouraged.
reference_source: Manual for Procurement of Works 2022 [SEEN]; 100% guarantee line [ASSUMPTION]
quote: Clause 32.1 Mobilization and Construction Machinery Advance Applicable No Mobilization and Construction Machinery
explanation: No mobilisation advance is given (No mobilisation and construction machinery advance is payable). You must fund mobilisation, site set-up and early materials from your own money until the first bill is paid.

title: Price variation with holes
rule: Raise when price variation leaves out labour, uses a long index lag, cuts off late-billed work, or applies only above a size or duration this contract does not reach.
value_found: applies only over Rs 10.00 crore; this contract is Rs 1.89 crore (contract value from the cash inputs)
reference_value: A full price variation covers labour and the main materials, uses recent indices and pays on all work done in the stipulated or extended period.
reference_source: Read from the contract's own clause (C5); lag line [ASSUMPTION]
quote: Price Adjustment shall be applicable only in case where the Amount in N.I.T. is more than Rs. 10 (Ten) Crores. This clause
explanation: Price variation is printed but does not apply to this contract: applies only over Rs 10.00 crore; this contract is Rs 1.89 crore (contract value from the cash inputs). Treat the contract as fixed price.
